questions.topic: Tests and taxes after the amendment
questions.learningObjective: interpret instructions to registrars about enrolment

stimulus.body: The registrar shall keep a separate list of the citizens who have applied to be enrolled, and shall assign to each such citizen a number. options.text: The instruction allowed any citizen to challenge the list of voters at the courthouse
options.misconception: invents a right of appeal that is absent

options.text: The instruction required every registrar to follow a printed questionnaire word for word
options.misconception: invents a uniform form the instruction does not require

options.text: The instruction set a fixed period of residence that a voter had to show before enrolment

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: A lease that depends on a vote
questions.learningObjective: explain how the share lease preserved old dependence after emancipation
questions.stem: Bee book, 11 April. The willows were green and I wrote out how the end of slavery changed the law of labour without changing the balance of power in the fields. Explain why the change from slavery to the share lease looked like freedom while producing much the same economic dependence.

answer.exemplar: A slave had no legal claim to the labour of his own and could not leave, while the worker on lease owned no land and could not take a crop with him, so the practical difference was small even where the legal difference was enormous. The land, the tools, the advances and the accounts all stayed with the landlord, and the share was only as good as the division made after the harvest. Freedom of contract was real in form and hollow in effect, and it left the worker in the same county with the same landlord and the same vote as before.

questions.explanation: The legal right to leave was the great gain, but the terms of the lease kept the worker dependent on the landlord's land, credit and counting. That is why emancipation did not produce the political independence its language promised.
questions.hint: Ask what the worker still could not take with him.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: A court declining to order a man counted
questions.learningObjective: explain the cost of a refusal to count a vote
questions.stem: Apiary notes, 8 June. The clover was in bloom and I drafted my account of the vote that was refused and what the refusal cost. Explain how a court that declined to order a man counted could be defended in law while defeating the purpose of the guarantee of 1870.

answer.exemplar: The amendment forbade the denial of the vote on account of race and left the details of registration, the poll book and the count to the states and the courts, so a decision turning on a question of procedure was formally consistent with the amendment. Its effect, however, was to let an exclusion operate without any finding of race, because the procedural defect stood in place of the real reason for the refusal. The cost fell on the citizen whose name was struck from the roll, since the vote was gone while the guarantee remained untouched on the page.

questions.explanation: A narrow reading of the guarantee let procedure decide cases that were about race in substance, and the man lost his vote while the amendment itself was never challenged. That is how the right was defeated without the right being repealed.
questions.hint: Ask what the amendment left to the states and the courts.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: Two answers to the question of the war's object
questions.learningObjective: explain why the border states stayed in the Union
questions.stem: Bee log, 17 May. The swarm settled in the pear tree and I wrote out the change in the war's stated object and its effect on the border states. Explain why the border states stayed in the Union even though their own legislatures had been asked to join the separation movement.

answer.exemplar: The border states with the largest populations of enslaved people had the most to lose from joining the movement, because a war to protect property in enslaved people left their own people in danger of being taken by the enrolling officers and by the armies that the movement would summon. Nor did the movement offer them anything they wanted, since their complaints about northern interference with the return laws could have been answered without leaving. Staying also let them hold out for a war fought to preserve the Union and the laws, which is what their loyalty to the Union had been proclaimed to mean in the first place.

questions.explanation: The border states had the largest stake in the fate of the people they held enslaved and nothing to gain from a movement that would not protect them, so they stayed even after their legislatures had been asked to leave. Their reasons were calculated rather than sentimental, which is why the war's object mattered so much to them.
questions.hint: Ask what a war to protect slavery would do to a slave state.

questions.topic: A lease that depends on a vote
questions.learningObjective: interpret a yearly settlement account under the lease

stimulus.body: The account of the crop for the year: the land yielded four hundred bushels of corn and eight bales of cotton. There was deducted the food and clothing advanced to the hands, the use of the mules and the tools, and the interest on the note given at planting time. The balance was divided between the parties according to the lease, and the note was carried forward with interest to the next year.

questions.stem: Garden apiary, 4 December. The bees were wrapped in straw and I read the account aloud. What does the account show about how the lease arrangement kept the worker in dependence?

options.text: The division was made before the advances were counted, so the worker received a share of the whole crop
options.misconception: reverses the order of deductions and division

options.text: Advances and interest were deducted before any share was divided, so the worker's share was what remained after charges he could not dispute
The note was paid off each year, so no debt was carried into the next planting
options.misconception: contradicts the account, which carries the note forward

options.text: The account was signed by three neighbours who witnessed the division
options.misconception: invents witnesses the account does not mention

questions.explanation: Deducting advances and interest before the division reduced the crop that was shared, and the balance of the note carried forward, so a bad year produced a claim rather than a loss. The arrangement was therefore self-renewing without any law requiring it.
questions.hint: Ask what was taken off before the crop was shared.

questions.learningObjective: draw a conclusion about why the dispute over the vote continued
questions.stem: Apiary notes, 22 December. The hive was wrapped for winter and I thought about the long dispute over the vote and what the courts did to it. Which conclusion best explains why the guarantee of 1870 failed to end the argument?

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: A legislature claiming the right to separate
questions.learningObjective: explain how a legislature justified a right the Constitution did not grant
questions.stem: Bee log, 14 February. The bees stirred in the mild weather and I drafted my answer about what the legislature was doing when it claimed the right to separate. Explain how a state legislature could claim to be acting for its people while asserting a right the Constitution did not grant it.

answer.exemplar: The legislature argued that the people of the state had been asked to consent to the Union, and that a body chosen by those people could judge whether the consent had been withdrawn, so the claim was made in the voice of the people and not of a faction. The difficulty is that the members of the Union were bound by the Constitution as a whole and had no procedure for releasing themselves, so the argument asserted a popular right against a legal order that gave no such right. It was a claim about where sovereignty rests, made to avoid the question of how a state could lawfully leave.

questions.explanation: By speaking for the people the legislature made the claim democratic in form, while the argument in substance rested on the idea that a state could nullify a constitutional arrangement for itself. That is a claim about sovereignty, and the other states answered it as a threat to their own constitutional standing.
questions.hint: Ask who the legislature said it was speaking for.

questions.topic: The result of a state's compliance
questions.learningObjective: interpret an address welcoming a restored state government

stimulus.body: Gentlemen: the authorities of the state are now restored, and the officers of the state will resume the functions of their offices. The legislature will assemble on the day appointed, and the constitution agreed upon by the people will be the law of the state from that day forward. The good people of the state are exhorted to go back to their accustomed labours, and the course of the commonwealth will be directed to the interests of all its citizens.

questions.stem: Hive log, 5 August. The honey was thin but the hive was strong and I copied the address into the book. What does the address show about what a state's compliance restored?

options.text: Federal control of the state's elections ended for ever on the day of the ceremony
options.misconception: reads a restoration of state authority as an end of federal authority

options.text: The state's own constitution, officers and legislature came back into operation, so government and lawmaking returned to the citizens of the state
The former officers of the old regime were returned to their posts

options.misconception: contradicts the reference to a constitution already agreed upon
